design_rationale: Participants were randomly allocated to treatment groups using sealed assignment envelopes administered by an unblinded pharmacist.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although sealed treatment assignment envelopes were used, the method of sequence generation is not described and it is not specified whether envelopes were sequentially numbered, opaque, or tamper-evident.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: After baseline GFR and ERPF measurements were obtained, an unblinded pharmacist with sealed treatment assignment envelopes randomized patients to receive 1/2 NS or 1/2 NS plus fenoldopam mesylate at 0.1 µg/kg/min.

domain_judgments.rationale: Double-blind conditions were maintained, but analysis was restricted to patients who completed all clearance measurements rather than a true intention-to-treat approach, with potential exclusions not fully accounted for.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: To maintain a double-blind format, the concentration of fenoldopam mesylate was adjusted to give 0.1 µg/kg/min at a constant infusion of 100 mL/h. ... Paraaminohippurate clearance data from patients who completed all preparaaminohippurate and postparaaminohippurate clearances were included in the statistical analyses.

domain_judgments.rationale: The study screened 51 patients and randomized 45 (22 vs 23), but it is not clearly reported how many participants completed all timed clearance measurements or whether any were excluded from the primary RPF analysis.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Paraaminohippurate clearance data from patients who completed all preparaaminohippurate and postparaaminohippurate clearances were included in the statistical analyses.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcomes were objective laboratory and physiological clearance measurements assessed under blinded conditions.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: For calculation of GFR and estimated RPF (ERPF), plasma paraaminohippurate levels were obtained before and after collection of 2 30-minute timed urine samples. ... To maintain a double-blind format, the concentration of fenoldopam mesylate was adjusted to give 0.1 µg/kg/min at a constant infusion of 100 mL/h.

domain_judgments.rationale: No pre-trial registration or published prospective protocol was cited to verify that reported analyses and time points adhered strictly to a pre-specified statistical analysis plan.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary endpoint was change in RPF 1 hour after contrast infusion. The secondary endpoint was incidence of RCN, defined as a 0.5 mg/dL or a 25% rise in serum creatinine level at 48 hours.

overall_summary: The study has some concerns overall due to insufficient reporting of sequence generation and envelope concealment procedures, complete-case restriction for physiological clearance measurements, and lack of a pre-registered statistical analysis protocol.

design_rationale: Participants were randomly assigned to fenoldopam or placebo using a computer-based random number generator.

domain_judgments.rationale: Allocation sequence was generated by computer and concealed via a central office and independent nurse coordinator, with well-balanced baseline characteristics.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Patients were randomly assigned to study groups using a computer-based random number generator. Code numbers were transmitted from the central office to the randomization authority of each center. This authority was a nurse not involved in the care of the trial patients who was responsible for preparation and distribution of trial drug infusion.

domain_judgments.rationale: The study was double-blind using indistinguishable syringes, and analysis adhered to the intention-to-treat principle with no reported protocol deviations.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Fenoldopam or placebo were prepared for syringe pump infusion in indistinguishable syringes... No patient, other nurse, investigator, or any other medical staff in ICU were aware of the treatment assignment for the duration of the study protocol.

domain_judgments.rationale: All 300 randomized patients were accounted for in the primary outcome analysis according to the trial profile and intention-to-treat analysis.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Of the remaining 300 patients, 150 were randomized to fenoldopam and 150 to placebo (Fig. 1)... We performed outcome analysis according to the intention-to-treat principle.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome is an objective laboratory measure (serum creatinine analyzed by a central biochemistry lab), and assessors/clinicians were fully blinded.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary outcome measure for the study was the incidence of ARF, defined as serum creatinine concentration >=150 mumol/L during trial drug infusion... Serum creatinine concentrations were analyzed daily by the central biochemistry laboratory.

domain_judgments.rationale: No prospective trial registry or pre-published statistical analysis plan is mentioned, leaving some concerns for selective reporting despite primary and secondary endpoints being explicitly defined in the methods.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary outcome measure for the study was the incidence of ARF, defined as serum creatinine concentration >=150 mumol/L during trial drug infusion. Secondary outcome measures included peak serum creatinine concentration...

overall_summary: The study is a well-designed, double-blind randomized controlled trial with robust randomization, concealment, and objective outcome assessment, but has some concerns overall due to the lack of an identifiable pre-registered protocol or analysis plan.

design_rationale: The study is described as a prospective, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial using computer-generated random allocation stratified by age.

domain_judgments.rationale: Computerized sequence generation and allocation concealment using sealed envelopes opened by an uninvolved nurse were appropriately executed, and baseline characteristics were balanced.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The allocation sequence was generated by using two computerized random-generation programs stratified by two age groups... sealed envelopes containing the allocation group were opened by a nurse who did not participate in the study or in data collection.

domain_judgments.rationale: Double-blind administration was maintained, no unblinded protocol deviations occurred aside from one accidental interruption analyzed via intention-to-treat, and care was standardized across groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The same nurse was in charge of preparing the infusions that were blindly given to the perfusionist. The rest of the nurses and medical staff in the operation room and in the intensive care unit were blinded to group assignment... Intention to treat (ITT) was applied, and all enrolled patients were considered for statistical analysis at the end of the study.

domain_judgments.rationale: Complete outcome data were available for all 80 randomized patients without any loss to follow-up.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Figure 1 depicts the flow chart of enrolment phases: in only one case was treatment interrupted by mistake (group P), but data from this patient were analyzed with ITT.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcomes were measured objectively via standard laboratory assays, and laboratory and clinical staff were blinded to group allocation.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: PCrea and uCrea levels were directly sent to the laboratory and measured with the Jaffe assay... Plasma and urinary NGAL were measured with a sandwich enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay... whereas plasma and urinary cystatin C were evaluated with nephelometry

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was registered prospectively and all pre-specified primary and secondary endpoints were reported in accordance with the pre-planned analysis strategy.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The study was approved by the local Ethics Committee... and was registered in the Protocol Registration System (Clinical Trial. Gov Id: NCT00982527). The primary end point of this study was to assess whether high-dose fenoldopam infusion during CPB affects renal function by perioperative urinary and plasma NGAL, CysC, and Crea levels measurement.

overall_summary: The trial was well-designed and conducted with adequate randomization and allocation concealment, robust double-blinding, complete follow-up of all participants, objective laboratory outcomes, and prospective registration with consistent reporting.

design_rationale: Participants were randomly allocated to one of three treatment arms using a random-allocation table.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although a random-allocation table was used to generate the sequence, no details are provided regarding allocation concealment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A random-allocation table was used to assign patients to one of the three arms of the study: intravenous (i.v.) saline only, i.v. saline plus N-acetylcysteine (NAC), or i.v. saline plus fenoldopam.

domain_judgments.rationale: The study was open-label without blinding of patients or personnel, and three patients in the fenoldopam group were excluded from the analysis rather than analyzed according to intention-to-treat principles.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A total of 126 patients were enrolled in the study; 123 patients completed the study as per the protocol. Three patients were withdrawn from the study as they developed hypotension due to fenoldopam.

domain_judgments.rationale: Data were available for 123 of 126 enrolled patients (97.6%), and the very small number of missing participants is unlikely to have meaningfully altered the findings.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A total of 126 patients were enrolled in the study; 123 patients completed the study as per the protocol. Three patients were withdrawn from the study as they developed hypotension due to fenoldopam.

domain_judgments.rationale: The outcome was defined by objective laboratory measurements of serum creatinine, which are standard and unlikely to be influenced by knowledge of intervention status.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: RCIN was defined as an absolute increase in serum creatinine level of at least 0.5 mg/dL within 48 hr of the injection of the radiocontrast medium.

domain_judgments.rationale: No prospective clinical trial registry or pre-published statistical analysis plan was cited, raising some concerns regarding potential selective reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All data were recorded using Microsoft Excel, then transferred to the Statistical Package for the Social Sciences (SPSS) program for statistical analysis. Data were analyzed using analysis of variance (ANOVA) and Bonferroni procedure.

overall_summary: The trial is rated as having some concerns overall due to lack of reported allocation concealment, post-randomization exclusion of patients without a full intention-to-treat analysis, and absence of a pre-registered protocol.

design_rationale: The study is described as a double-blind randomized clinical trial where allocation was generated by a computer list and contained in sealed envelopes.
overall_summary: The overall judgment is some concerns, primarily driven by incomplete details on allocation concealment (sealed envelopes without specified opacity or sequential numbering) and lack of a pre-registered trial protocol or analysis plan.

design_rationale: Participants were randomly allocated 1:1 using computer-generated concealed block randomization schedules maintained by research pharmacists.

domain_judgments.rationale: Allocation sequence was generated with block randomization, central concealment was maintained by independent research pharmacists, and baseline characteristics were well-balanced.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Two concealed randomization schedules (for diabetic and nondiabetic patients), each in blocks of 6, were prepared by the sponsor and maintained by a research pharmacist at each site. When informed an eligible patient had been enrolled, the research pharmacist allocated the patient to the next sequential randomization number.

domain_judgments.rationale: Double-blind study using matching placebo with successful blinding of participants and caregivers, and an intention-to-treat approach was used.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All caregivers, trial participants, patients, and committee members were blinded to the group assignment, with the exception of (1) the research pharmacist, who had no patient care responsibilities and who did not interact with other study participants and (2) select personnel from the sponsor for purposes of performing drug accountability... Unless otherwise stated, all analyses were by intention to treat

domain_judgments.rationale: Missing outcome data accounted for approximately 10% of patients evenly across groups (20/157 vs 12/158), with sensitivity analyses demonstrating robustness of the findings.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary study end point of contrast-induced nephropathy could not be determined in approximately 10% of patients in whom serial creatinine measurements were not available. Most of these patients were asymptomatic as outpatients and declined returning to the clinic for blood draws. Moreover, the baseline characteristics were similar in patients with vs without follow-up creatinine assessment, and the principal results were unchanged in sensitivity analyses when these patients were imputed either as developing or not developing contrast-induced nephropathy.

domain_judgments.rationale: The outcome was objectively determined by laboratory measurement of serum creatinine by a central biochemistry laboratory blinded to treatment assignment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Blood samples were scheduled to be drawn and sent to a central biochemistry laboratory for serum creatinine measurements after the prestudy drug hydration period (but before study drug administration) and at 24 hours (or at the time of discharge, if earlier), 48 to 60 hours, and 72 to 96 hours following the completion of study drug administration.

domain_judgments.rationale: The reported results align with the pre-specified primary and secondary endpoints and statistical analysis plan outlined in the methods.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary efficacy end point was the development of contrast-induced nephropathy, defined as an increase in serum creatinine level of 25% or more from baseline to the maximum value obtained within the 24- to 96-hour period following completion of study drug administration. Additional efficacy end points included measurements of contrast-induced nephropathy defined as 2 consecutive increases in serum creatinine level of 25% or more, and an increase in serum creatinine level of 0.5 mg/dL (44.2 µmol/L) or more.

overall_summary: This study was a rigorously conducted, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled multicenter trial with low risk of bias across all five RoB 2 domains.

design_rationale: Patients were randomly allocated to one of three treatment arms (fenoldopam, dopamine, or placebo) using sealed envelopes.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although allocation was concealed using unmarked sealed envelopes arranged by independent staff, the exact sequence generation method is not specified, though baseline characteristics are well balanced.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Before undergoing surgery, the patients were randomized to one of the following intravenous treatments using unmarked, sealed envelopes containing the group allocation (the order of the envelopes was determined blindly by a member of the Department’s secretarial staff who played no other role in the study)

domain_judgments.rationale: ICU physicians were blinded, patients were under anesthesia/sedation in the ICU, care protocols were standardized across groups, and all enrolled participants received their assigned intervention without crossovers.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The ICU physicians were not aware of which group the patients had been randomized to... There was no therapy crossover between the groups, nor was it necessary to discontinue any of the study drugs at any time because of the occurrence of adverse events potentially attributable to them.

domain_judgments.rationale: Only 4 of 144 patients (2.8%) were excluded due to incomplete collections, representing very low missing outcome data that is unlikely to bias the results.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: This study involved a population of 144 consecutive subjects who underwent OLT at our Centre between January 2001 and July 2003; 4 were excluded because of incomplete sample collections. The analysis was therefore based on 140 patients: 46 in group P (placebo), 48 in group D (dopamine), and 46 in group F (fenoldopam).

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcomes (creatinine, creatinine clearance, diuresis) are objective laboratory measurements, and attending ICU physicians assessing patients were blinded.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Daily postoperative serum creatinine levels. Postoperative creatinine clearance (calculated every 12 hours by means of the simultaneous collection of blood and urine samples, the latter from continuous collections).

domain_judgments.rationale: All outcomes and time points defined in the protocol and methods section are reported in full without evidence of selective outcome reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The following variables were recorded during the study (the postoperative data collection lasted 96 hours)... Absolute changes from baseline in serum creatinine and creatinine clearance levels 24, 48, 72 and 96 hours after the end of surgery.

overall_summary: The overall risk of bias is rated as some concerns due to Domain 1, as the specific method of random sequence generation was not described even though allocation concealment was used and baseline characteristics were balanced. All other domains had low risk of bias.

design_rationale: Participants were randomly allocated to fenoldopam or placebo using a computerized random number generation program with block randomization managed by the hospital pharmacy.

domain_judgments.rationale: Allocation sequence was generated by computer, concealed using pharmacy-held sealed envelopes, and baseline characteristics between groups were balanced.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The random allocation sequence was generated using a computerized random generation program. The randomization was generated in blocks of 20 patients. This procedure was performed by an external staff person working in the hospital pharmacy. Based on this process, sealed envelopes containing the allocation group were created and stored in the pharmacy.

domain_judgments.rationale: Patients, healthcare personnel, and outcome assessors were blinded using identical unlabeled bottles, and analysis followed intention-to-treat without substantial protocol deviations.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The participants, those administering the drug, and those assessing the outcomes were blinded to group assignment... The pharmacist prepared either drug or placebo according to the randomization sequence, using unlabeled 500 mL bottles.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data were available for all randomized patients for the primary endpoints, and the pre-specified exclusion of two chronic dialysis patients from renal endpoints was fully documented and unlikely to bias the results.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Two patients with chronic renal failure under dialytic treatment in the fenoldopam group were excluded from the analysis of secondary endpoints related to changes in renal function and AKI incidence.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcomes were objective laboratory and physiological parameters (blood lactate, oxygen delivery, serum creatinine) measured identically across groups with blinded outcome assessors.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The participants, those administering the drug, and those assessing the outcomes were blinded to group assignment... The primary endpoint of this study was to assess if fenoldopam infusion during prolonged CPB resulted in changes to the adequacy of perfusion, as established by serial measurements of blood lactate (BL) concentration and oxygen delivery (DO ) during CPB.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered on ClinicalTrials.gov and reported pre-specified primary and secondary outcomes according to the planned protocol.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The study was approved by the local Ethics Committee and was registered in the Protocol Registration System Clinical Trial.Gov (registration number NCT00747331).

overall_summary: The study is a well-designed, prospective, double-blind, randomized placebo-controlled trial with low risk of bias across all RoB 2 domains, including adequate random sequence generation, allocation concealment, blinding, complete data reporting, and prospective registration.
